title: Posters
text:
Poster Guidelines
We encourage all AAGI Symposium participants to prepare a poster showcasing their research, project, tools, or area of work. The poster session provides an opportunity to share ideas, highlight your work, and foster discussion and collaboration across the AAGI community.

Poster submission
Submission deadline: 20 October 2026
This deadline allows sufficient time for posters to be printed in Perth and ensures they are ready for display at the symposium.


Submission process
Poster submission involves two steps:
1. Complete the Google Form
The Google form collects your poster details and a few questions about the poster showcase. A confirmation email will be sent to the email address you provide.
Submit Your Poster Details ↗
2. Upload your poster to Box
Use the Box link to upload your PDF poster. You do not need a Box account to upload a file.
Upload Your Poster ↗



File requirements

Format: PDF
File name: Please use the following format: Poster_SurnameFirstName.pdf

Example: Poster_SmithJohn.pdf

Number of posters: One poster per participant. Collaborative group posters are encouraged where a project has multiple contributors.





Poster content
Posters should clearly communicate:

The research, project, tool, or area of work being presented.
The problem, question, or objective being addressed.
The methods, approach, or workflow used.
Key findings, outcomes, or expected impacts (where available).
Contact details to enable follow-up discussions and collaboration.



Poster format

Size: A0 (841 × 1189 mm)
Orientation: Portrait

Posters will be displayed on double-sided poster boards, with two A0 portrait posters displayed on each side.


QR code
Please include a QR code placeholder on your poster. This will be used to link to the digital version of your poster on the symposium website. A minimum size of 8 × 8 cm is recommended to ensure the QR code can be scanned easily.


Short poster presentations
PhD students will be invited to give a brief 3-5 minute “elevator pitch” alongside their poster. This is an opportunity to introduce yourself, provide a concise overview of your project, highlight its significance, and encourage further discussion during the poster session. Subject to available time, researchers who opt in may also be invited to give a short poster presentation.


Poster awards
Poster awards will be presented at the conclusion of the symposium. Further details regarding award categories, judging criteria, and assessment processes will be provided closer to the event.

title: HDR Networking Session
section: Shaping the Future of Agritech Research
text:
Shaping the Future of Agritech Research
This interactive networking session will focus on three core pillars:

Career Development: Navigating pathways across academia, industry, and government, securing funding, and understanding what modern employers value.
Industry Engagement: Exploring AI applications in agriculture and discovering how industry internships can complement doctoral research.
Mentoring & Networking: Building connections with peers, senior researchers, and industry professionals to foster collaboration and support.

Our goal is to kickstart an ongoing, collaborative HDR community within AAGI that continues to share opportunities, experiences, and advice long after the symposium concludes.

text:
Venue and Attendee Resources

Venue map

QT Perth: 133 Murray Street, Perth WA



Wi-Fi details

Wi-Fi network and password will be available at the venue and shared with attendees during the symposium.



Accessibility and transport (Perth Domestic Airport to QT Perth)

Taxi or rideshare: approximately 20 to 30 minutes, depending on traffic.
Public transport: typically 45 to 60 minutes (bus + train + short walk).
Recommended drop-off point: QT Perth main entrance on Murray Street.



Local logistics

Parking: use nearby CBD public parking stations (rates and availability vary).
Nearby food: multiple cafes and restaurants within short walking distance on Murray Street and Hay Street.
Emergency contacts:

Emergency services (Police, Fire, Ambulance): 000
Police assistance (non-urgent): 131 444
Healthdirect: 1800 022 222
